title: Mathematics on arXiv — weekly notable papers, 2–9 October 2026
global_caveat: This is an inferred notable-paper selection, not an official arXiv popularity ranking. Citation totals are only 0–1 for these new papers and are too sparse to measure within-week attention; mathematical claims are preprint claims and have not been peer reviewed here.

sections.title: The Exact Overlaps Conjecture for Self-Similar Measures on the Real Line
sections.abstract: For finitely supported contracting similarities of the real line, the authors claim the self-similar measure has dimension min(1, h_mu/|chi_mu|), establishing the exact-overlaps conjecture and its generalized dimension formula in dimension one.
sections.claimed_result: The authors' Theorem 1.1 gives dim nu = min{1, h_mu/|chi_mu|} for a probability measure on a finite family of contracting similarities of R; they say this yields the exact-overlaps criterion and a self-similar-set dimension formula when there are no exact overlaps.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A finite family of contracting similarities on R with positive weights; h_mu is random-walk entropy and chi_mu the Lyapunov exponent.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is specifically one-dimensional. The paper notes another public manuscript independently announced the theorem; expert comparison is needed to resolve the relationship between proofs.

sections.title: Abundance for threefolds in positive characteristic
sections.abstract: The authors claim the abundance conjecture for projective log-canonical threefold pairs over perfect fields of characteristic greater than 42.
sections.claimed_result: If (X,B) is a projective lc pair of dimension 3 over a perfect field of characteristic p > 42 and K_X+B is nef, then the authors prove it is semi-ample.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Three-dimensional projective lc pairs over perfect fields, with characteristic p > 42 and nef log-canonical divisor.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors call this a very preliminary version, identify an irregular-boundary case as still open, and say a companion paper is forthcoming. The theorem does not cover all positive characteristics.

sections.title: Sharp dynamical isoperimetric principle for mean curvature flow
sections.abstract: For weak mean-curvature flows starting from a smooth bounded domain, the authors give sharp extinction-time and space-time isoperimetric bounds, with equality only for the round shrinking sphere.
sections.claimed_result: The paper bounds extinction time by (1/(2n))(P(Ω)/|S^n|)^(2/n) for level-set and integral Brakke flows, with equality only for a round ball and its standard multiplicity-one shrinking sphere; it also gives a sharp parabolic-measure inequality.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Euclidean R^(n+1), smooth bounded initial domain and the specified weak-flow notions; arrival-time estimates separately assume mean convexity.
sections.unique_caveat: The sharp statements concern specified weak formulations and smooth initial boundaries, not arbitrary initial sets or geometric flows.

sections.title: The circle packing and Riemann uniformization embedding of the tree-weighted planar maps converges to Liouville quantum gravity
sections.abstract: The authors claim that spanning-tree-weighted planar maps converge under circle-packing and Riemann-uniformization embeddings to the corresponding sqrt(2)-Liouville quantum-gravity surfaces, with an associated path converging to SLE_8.
sections.claimed_result: In disk, sphere and whole-plane topologies, the embedded maps converge respectively to a sqrt(2)-LQG disk, sphere and cone as the number of faces grows; the natural path on map faces converges to SLE_8.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Spanning-tree-weighted random planar maps in the named topologies and discrete conformal embeddings; the proof combines earlier convergence results and a companion embedding comparison.
sections.unique_caveat: This concerns a particular tree-weighted map model and builds on companion/prior work; it does not establish the same limit for planar maps in general.

sections.title: The LeBrun–Salamon conjecture is true in dimension up to 56
sections.abstract: The authors claim the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture for positive quaternionic-Kähler manifolds of quaternionic dimension at most 14 (real dimension at most 56), using symmetry-rank and characteristic-number arguments.
sections.claimed_result: For positive quaternionic-Kähler manifolds with quaternionic dimension n ≤ 14, the authors rule out a minimal counterexample by bounding its isometry group and showing a related characteristic-number index is positive.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Positive quaternionic-Kähler manifolds restricted to quaternionic dimension at most 14.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a finite-dimensional range, not a proof in all dimensions. The paper mentions partial Lean verification, which is not equivalent to independent mathematical review of the full argument.

sections.title: Navier-Stokes lost in translation: Why Lean verification of AI autoformalisation does not guarantee correct natural language proofs
sections.abstract: The authors argue that a mechanically checked Lean proof can fail to validate the natural-language argument it was meant to formalize, and give examples including a claimed Navier–Stokes blow-up proof.
sections.claimed_result: The authors formulate ambiguity resolution in natural-language mathematics as having unbounded Solvability Complexity Index/arithmetical hierarchy complexity, and argue that the cited Lean verification does not correspond to the natural-language Navier–Stokes argument.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A theoretical analysis of semantic faithfulness in translating mathematical natural language into formal statements, with case studies.
sections.unique_caveat: This is the authors' analysis of formalization fidelity and selected examples, not a resolution of Navier–Stokes regularity or a general audit of all AI-generated proofs.
